other_measurements.label: Baseline BCVA
named: The presenting best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and intraocular pressure (IOP) were recorded.
The Snellen visual acuity was converted into a logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution i.e. logMAR for statistical analysis.
result: The mean BCVA in group A and B was logMAR 0.79 ± 0.24 (Snellen equivalent 20/123) and logMAR 0.75 ± 0.22 (Snellen equivalent 20/112) respectively (p = 0.471) (Table 1).

other_measurements.label: BCVA at day 1 and 2 weeks
named: Post-operative visits were scheduled at day1, 2 weeks, 1 month and 6 months.
At each follow-up visit BCVA, IOP and SD-OCT were recorded.
second_look: Mean BCVA at post-operative 1-month in Group A and Group B was logMAR 0.68 ± 0.25 (Snellen equivalent 20/96) and logMAR 0.54 ± 0.19 (Snellen equivalent 20/69) (p = 0.016) respectively.

other_measurements.label: BCVA at 6 months
named: The main outcome measures were anatomical and visual outcome at the end of 6 months.
At each follow-up visit BCVA, IOP and SD-OCT were recorded.
result: Mean BCVA at post-operative 6-month in Group A and B was logMAR 0.65 ± 0.25 (Snellen equivalent 20/89) and logMAR 0.53 ± 0.20 (Snellen equivalent 20/68) respectively (p = 0.060).

other_measurements.label: Change in BCVA from pre- to post-operative
named: Wilcoxon sign rank test was used to find out the difference between pre- and post-operative visual acuity.
result: The mean improvement in BCVA was 1.4 and 2.1 lines in groups A and B respectively (p = 0.353) (Table 2).

planned: Student’s t-test/ Mann-Whitney U test was used to find out the significant difference of continuous variables between the two study groups.
reported: Mean BCVA at post-operative 1-month in Group A and Group B was logMAR 0.68 ± 0.25 (Snellen equivalent 20/96) and logMAR 0.54 ± 0.19 (Snellen equivalent 20/69) (p = 0.016) respectively.
